title: Science of the Courtiers of This Century
text:
To bathe one's mane with flour,

to go showing everyone one's shirt,

a sword that does not frighten but provokes laughter,

one's ring, one's watch, and one's chain;


to speak to everyone with a serene face,

to kiss Doña Luisa's feet at mass,

and to attend, as a very necessary matter,

condolence, pleasure, and congratulations;


to be in love with oneself,

to mumble an aria in Italian,

and to dance in French, crooked or straight;


with this, and forgetting the catechism,

behold yourself made a proper courtier,

but the devil will carry you off, said and done.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's recipe-like mockery of fashionable courtly behavior.

title: The Powerful Man Swallows Rich Soup...
text:
The powerful man swallows rich soup

while I am content with dregs;

and though the world is a vast map,

to his vice it seems a narrow cup.


With embroidered, subtle, soft clothing

he diligently covers human clay;

while a miserable cloak wraps me

and a black shirt of rough tow.


He displays to all his gouty belly,

and the filthy wineskin may taste better to me

than his pipe does to him.


Fleeing human misery he climbs;

but, however much he bids, walks, and gasps,

we are all clusters from one vine.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the social contrast between luxury and poverty before returning both to one human vine.

title: The House of a Grandee
editorial_note: The translation keeps the household inventory as a satirical anatomy of aristocratic vice.

title: Court Thieves
text:
I hear many courtiers say:

that office has three thousand reales,

but it is worth ten thousand, very exact-

God help me, and they flog Gypsies!


Those are vulgar petty thieves

who steal a cloak, some swaddling clothes,

a donkey, a mule, and their funds;

they do not amount to six Segovian quarters.


You inspect the mountains; it is a chimera,

for thieves are not hermits,

nor do they seek their career in thickets.


Let justice make inquiries here,

and it will see that the Court is a burrow

where they are nested in heaps.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the historical slur in context while keeping the poem's attack on elite theft.

title: Lost Love
text:
The child dearest to Venus went out

to his accustomed gentle conquest,

and, delayed in returning to his dwelling,

his beautiful mother took him for lost.


She goes out, runs, asks after Cupid,

impatient, anxious, frightened,

color withered, hair disheveled;

in Cyprus she sought him, in Paphos and Cnidus.


She seeks him among the nymphs she venerates

as most beautiful, in forest, river, meadow;

she seeks him among the nymphs the sea breeds.


She touched the bank of Father Tormes,

and found him here, hanging from the snowy

neck of most beautiful María.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the playful mythological search for Cupid ending at María's neck by the Tormes.
